bug_semantics: picklescan is a pickle malware scanner whose infection verdict (issues_count, CLI exit 1) is driven only by an explicit denylist of GLOBAL imports. torch.utils._config_module.ConfigModule.load_config pickle.loads attacker-supplied bytes, so a REDUCE to that callable embeds a nested malicious pickle that executes during pickle.load. Until 0.0.28 the GLOBAL (torch.utils._config_module, ConfigModule.load_config) was absent from the denylist, so the scanner labeled it Suspicious rather than Dangerous, left issues_count at 0, and exited 0; a victim who trusted the scan would then load the file and run the inner payload.
flaw_origin: c1d5abdcc740e0d08a0d12d015d08e1e6f29a67e (2022-09-04, 'Implement Pickle scanner') first wrote src/picklescan/scanner.py with _suspicious_globals and matching that increments issues_count only when the imported module/name is on that finite list. Immediate parent 6a76b8c3ac67dc04181e600614ecf2a423cca326 has no scanner.py. Later work renamed the map to _unsafe_globals and classified unlisted names as SafetyLevel.Suspicious, but preserved the fail-open 'unlisted is not Dangerous / not an issue' policy. The load_config gadget was never listed until the 0.0.28 denylist patch.
